name: Women's Rights
description: Women's rights from the first demands for equality to the vote, the workplace and #MeToo: the people, campaigns and laws.

checkpoints.name: The first demands
checkpoints.note: Mary Wollstonecraft argues for women's education. At Seneca Falls in 1848 women demand the vote.

checkpoints.name: Votes for women
checkpoints.note: New Zealand gives women the vote in 1893. Suffragettes march and are jailed in Britain, and women win the vote in many countries after the First World War.

checkpoints.name: Equality at work and home
checkpoints.note: Simone de Beauvoir and Betty Friedan inspire a second wave of feminism. Laws and a UN treaty promise equal rights.

checkpoints.name: Today
checkpoints.note: Malala survives an attack for going to school, and the MeToo movement spreads across the world.
